Short description: Raise weights in a broad outward arc from in front of your body toward overhead.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 5–8 repetitions with very light weights and a comfortable range.

Short description: Rotate the wrists during an overhead pressing sequence as described in the article.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 5–8 slow repetitions with very light weights, after learning the movement.

Short description: Stand with knees slightly bent and hinge forward slightly. Reach one arm forward beside your ear while extending the other behind you. Return and alternate sides.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: No dose listed. Suggested general-audience starting dose: 1 set of 8–10 controlled repetitions per side.

Short description: Extend your arms sideways at shoulder height. Make forward circles, then backward circles.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 10 forward circles and 10 backward circles. The article then says “Repeat this 10 times total!” without clarifying whether this means 10 rounds.

Short description: Press dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms outward, then reverse.
Hinge forward and lift your arms outward to emphasize the rear shoulders.
Raise weights in front of your body to approximately shoulder height, then lower.
From a wall-supported handstand, move your hands away from the wall while walking your feet downward.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3 sets; rest 30 seconds between sets. The article lists “10m high” as the repetition prescription; this is unclear and should not be treated as an actionable dose.

Short description: Raise your arms out to the sides to just below shoulder height, then lower.
Equipment needed: Dumbbells, cable machine, or lateral raise machine

Short description: Perform a standing overhead press with your feet together and trunk braced.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–10 repetitions with a light load.

Short description: Begin in a high plank with shoulders over wrists. Lift your hips up and back into an inverted V, inhale, then exhale as you return to plank.
Press weights overhead from shoulder height, then lower.
Equipment needed: Dumbbells, kettlebells, barbell, or shoulder press machine

Short description: Lift a weight upward close to your torso by raising your elbows, then lower within a comfortable range.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–10 repetitions with a light load.
Equipment needed: Dumbbells, barbell, Smith machine, or cable machine

Short description: Curl one dumbbell at a time, rotating the palm upward as you lift.
Keep your upper arms near your sides and curl weights toward your shoulders, then lower.
Support yourself on parallel dip bars. Bend your elbows to lower until they reach approximately a right angle, then press upward.
Curl dumbbells while keeping your palms facing inward.
Place your hands on one bench and feet on another; bend and straighten your elbows to lower and raise your body.
Lie on a bench with arms raised; bend and straighten your elbows while keeping your upper arms relatively still.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–12 repetitions with a light load.

Short description: Bench press with a narrower hand position to emphasize the triceps.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–10 repetitions with a light load.

Short description: Hold a weight overhead, bend your elbows to lower it behind your head, then straighten your arms.
Equipment needed: Dumbbell, barbell, cable machine, or extension machine

Short description: Rest your upper arms on an angled pad and bend your elbows to curl the weight upward.
Equipment needed: Preacher bench and dumbbells or barbell; alternatively a preacher curl machine

Short description: Sit on the floor with hands behind you and fingers pointing toward your buttocks. Lift your hips, bend your elbows backward to lower, then straighten your arms.
Hinge forward with your upper arm beside your torso; straighten the elbow backward, then bend it again.
Equipment needed: Dumbbell or cable machine; optional support bench

Short description: Curl with palms upward, rotate to palms downward at the top, then lower slowly.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–10 repetitions with light weights.

Short description: Hinge forward and pull a weight toward your abdomen, then lower.
Equipment needed: Dumbbells, barbell, Smith machine, or T-bar machine

Short description: From a high plank, lift one hand and pull that elbow toward your ribs, squeezing your upper back. Replace the hand and alternate sides. Modify by keeping your knees down.
Lie face down and gently raise your upper torso, then lower.
Stand with knees slightly bent, hinge forward at your hips, then return upright.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–10 repetitions, initially without added weight.

Short description: Stand with arms reaching overhead, shoulder-width apart. Pretend to grasp a bar and pull your elbows down and out, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Return overhead.
Stand with knees slightly bent and hinge forward about 45 degrees. With arms hanging down, raise them out to the sides to shoulder height, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then lower.
Raise your shoulders toward your ears against resistance, then lower.
Perform a controlled hip hinge with legs kept nearly straight.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 6–8 repetitions with a light load and a comfortable range.

Short description: Lie face down with arms extended forward. Lift your arms, legs, and chest slightly off the floor, pause, then lower.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–10 repetitions, briefly pausing at the top.

Short description: Lie face down with arms overhead. Lift your head, shoulders, and arms, then sweep your straight arms outward and back toward your hips. Reverse the sweep without lowering between repetitions.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 6–10 slow repetitions. One complete backward-and-forward arm sweep equals 1 repetition.

Short description: Hang from a bar with palms facing away and hands comfortably wider than shoulder-width. Pull your chin above the bar, then lower with control.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 3–5 controlled repetitions, only if able to perform them with good form.

Short description: Lie on a bench and press a weight upward from your chest.
Equipment needed: Bench and dumbbells, barbell with rack, or press machine

Short description: Lower into a press-up, then push explosively so your hands leave the floor. Tap your chest before landing back on your hands.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 3–5 repetitions, only for those already proficient in explosive press-ups.

Short description: Bring your outstretched arms together in front of your chest against resistance.
Equipment needed: Dumbbells and bench, cable machine, or pec deck

Short description: Start in a high plank and lower your body to the floor. Briefly lift your hands, replace them, and press back up. Modify by keeping your knees down during the push-up.
Perform a bench press with the bar lowered toward the neck rather than the usual chest position.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: No general-audience dose provided; obtain qualified instruction before attempting this variation.
Equipment needed: Bench, barbell, rack, and appropriate spotting

Short description: Hold a high plank with hands beneath shoulders. Lower your chest close to the floor, then press back up while keeping your body straight.
Begin in a high plank with shoulders over wrists. Bend your elbows about 45 degrees from your body, pause just above the floor, then press back up.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 5–10 repetitions; pause for 1 second at the bottom.

Short description: Stand at arm’s length from a wall with palms against it at chest height and fingers pointing up. Keep your back straight and elbows beside your body as you bend your arms toward the wall, then slowly push back.
Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Tuck your toes, engage your core, and hover your knees a few inches above the floor.

Activity Name: Criss Cross & Reach with Knees Up
Short description: Lie on your back with knees raised and bent to 90 degrees. Press your palms together at your chest, curl upward, and reach across one thigh. Return to center and alternate sides.
Lie on your back with knees bent and curl your shoulders toward your pelvis.
Lie on your back with legs raised and knees bent to 90 degrees. Place hands behind your head, curl upward, and draw your elbows toward your knees. Lower to the starting position.
Place your forearms on the floor, brace your abdomen, and support yourself on your forearms and toes with your body in a straight line. Modify by resting your knees on the floor.
Lie with arms and legs extended. Raise your torso and legs together, reach toward your feet, and hold the V-shaped position.

Activity Name: Modified Side Plank Elbow to Knee
Short description: From kneeling, place one hand on the floor to your side with the shoulder above the wrist. Extend the opposite leg to hip height, put the free hand behind your head, and crunch that elbow toward the raised thigh.
Start in a high plank with your core engaged. Alternate bringing your knees toward your chest while maintaining a controlled trunk position.
Lie on your back with knees bent. Curl one shoulder upward and rotate its elbow toward the opposite knee, then lower slowly.
Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms extended overhead. Contract your abdomen to lift your shoulders while keeping your arms aligned with your upper body.
Lie on your back with arms beside you. Draw your knees toward your chest and curl your pelvis to lift your hips, then lower slowly.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 5 sets of 60 seconds, as part of the article’s abdominal circuit.

Short description: Hold a forearm plank while tucking your pelvis, squeezing your glutes, and strongly engaging your abdominal muscles.
Sit with knees bent and torso leaning backward; rotate your trunk from side to side.
Hold a high plank with shoulders over wrists. Shift your weight to one hand and tap the opposite shoulder with the other hand. Alternate sides.
Lie on your side supported on one forearm. Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line, hold, then repeat on the other side.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3 sets of 4 repetitions; rest 30 seconds between sets. The article does not specify a hold duration or whether the count is per side.

Short description: Lie on your back with one foot on the floor and the other leg extended toward the ceiling. Keep your lower back pressed down as you lower the raised leg about 45 degrees, then lift it again.
Lie on your back with arms and legs reaching upward. Curl your head and neck up, lower one leg, and reach toward the toes of the leg that remains raised. Return and alternate sides.
From a high plank, bring one knee toward the elbow on the same side. Pause, return, and alternate sides.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3 sets of 10 repetitions total, 5 per side; rest 60 seconds between sets.

Short description: From a high plank, move your hands and feet outward into an X shape. Brace your abdomen and hold your body straight.
Lie on your back with legs extended toward the ceiling. Reach toward your feet while lifting your head, neck, and shoulders, then lower your upper body.
Curl your upper body while bringing one shoulder toward the opposite side.
Support your body upright with legs hanging, then raise your knees toward your chest.
Lift a weight from the floor by extending your hips and knees, then lower with control.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 6–8 repetitions with a light load.
Equipment needed: Barbell, dumbbells, trap bar, or Smith machine

Short description: Using the article’s bench-based instructions, lie with your hips at the bench edge and legs extended beyond it. Squeeze your glutes and alternate small leg lifts.
Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms beside you. Squeeze your glutes to lift your hips, pause, then lower.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 10 repetitions; hold at the top for 1 second each time.

Short description: Start on hands and knees. Lift one leg backward until the thigh aligns with your back, squeeze your glutes, then lower and alternate.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–12 repetitions per side; hold for 1 second at the top.

Short description: Stand with hands behind your head and knees slightly bent. Hinge forward at your hips with your core engaged and back straight, pause, then return upright.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–12 repetitions; pause for 1 second in the hinged position.

Short description: From a high plank, jump your feet forward beside your hands, then return to the starting position.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, heels about 6–8 inches from your buttocks. Raise your hips, squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
Stand upright holding the back of a chair. Lift one straight leg backward without arching your back, then lower. Repeat with the other leg.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: Hold each lift for up to 5 seconds; 5 repetitions per leg.

Short description: Lie on the floor and raise your legs toward vertical, then lower with control.
Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your chest, then return with control.
Sit on a bench and lift your knees or legs toward your torso.
Lie on your side and raise the upper leg, then lower.
Hold the back of a chair. Raise one leg out to the side as far as comfortable, keeping your back and hips straight without leaning sideways. Lower and repeat with the other leg.
Balance on one leg with its knee softly bent. Hinge forward as the opposite leg lifts behind you, reaching toward the standing foot or shin. Return upright and repeat on both sides.
Lie on your back with one foot planted and the other leg raised. Lift your hips, squeeze the supporting-side glute, then lower slowly.

Activity Name: Standing Leg Lift to the Back
Short description: Stand on one leg with the other extended behind you. Draw your abdomen inward and lift the straight back leg using your glutes.
Deadlift with a wider stance and your hands inside your legs.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 6–8 repetitions with a light load.

Short description: Step forward and bend both knees partway into a shallow lunge. Continue traveling forward with alternating half lunges.
Lower into a squat and stand using your body weight only.
Squat onto a stable box or bench, pause briefly, then stand.
Equipment needed: Stable box or bench; optional weights

Short description: Rest your rear foot on a bench, bend the front leg to lower, then stand.
Squat while supporting a weight across the front of your shoulders.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 8–10 repetitions with a light load.

Short description: Lower into a squat, jump upward, then land softly into the next squat.
Lower into a lunge, jump, and switch leg positions in the air. Land in the opposite lunge and repeat with control.
Step into a split stance, bend both knees to lower, then return.
Hold the back of a chair with feet hip-width apart. Slowly bend your knees as far as comfortable, keeping your back straight and knees facing forward. Return to standing, squeezing your buttocks.
Balance on one leg with the other extended forward. Push your hips back, lower into a single-leg squat, then rise.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3 sets of 14 repetitions; rest 30 seconds between sets. The workout defines one repetition as completing both legs.

Short description: From standing, step one foot backward and bend both knees, lowering until the front knee is about 90 degrees. Return to standing and alternate sides.
Step sideways into a lunge, then push back to center. Lift that knee toward your chest and twist your torso toward it while balancing on the other leg.

Sit near the edge of a chair with feet hip-width apart. Lean slightly forward and stand slowly using your legs rather than your arms. Stand upright, then slowly sit down, using your hands only to guide you if possible.
Bend your hips and knees to lower, then return to standing; optionally hold weights.
Lower into a squat. Stand through your heels and lift one knee toward your chest. Return to the squat and alternate knees.
Bend into a squat, swing your arms, and jump forward. Land with control before resetting.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3 sets of 8 repetitions; rest 30 seconds between sets.

Short description: Place one foot on a stable bench or box. Push through that foot to stand on the platform, then step down and alternate sides.
Equipment needed: Stable exercise step, bench, or box

Short description: Hinge forward with only a slight knee bend, then extend your hips to stand.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 6–8 repetitions with a light load.

Short description: Step forward and lower your back knee toward the floor. Push through the front foot to stand and continue forward with the opposite leg.
Start in a squat with feet hip-width apart. Step sideways into a wider squat, then bring the trailing foot toward the leading foot while staying low.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 10 sideways steps in one direction, then repeat in the opposite direction.

Short description: Rest your back against a wall and lower into a static squat.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: Hold as long as possible; no specific duration listed.
Equipment needed: Wall; optional exercise ball behind the back

Short description: Hold the back of a chair. Slowly lift both heels off the floor as far as comfortable, then lower with control. Perform without support to make it more difficult.
Hinge forward with supported upper body and raise your heels against resistance.
Equipment needed: Donkey calf raise machine or suitable supported setup

Short description: Sit with resistance resting above your knees; lift and lower your heels.
Equipment needed: Seated calf raise machine or padded weight and stable seat

Short description: Raise and lower your heel while balancing on one leg.
Raise your heels to stand on the balls of your feet, then lower.
Start on hands and toes with knees hovering under your hips. Travel forward by moving one hand and the opposite foot together, keeping your hips level.
Squat down, place your hands on the floor, and move your feet back into a plank. Bring your feet forward, stand, and jump.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3 sets of 20 repetitions; rest 30 seconds between sets.

Short description: Perform a burpee with your chest lowering to the floor. Return to standing, then swing your arms and jump forward before repeating.
Lift a barbell to the shoulders, then drive it overhead.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3–5 technique repetitions with an unloaded training bar, under qualified instruction.
Equipment needed: Training bar or barbell; suitable lifting area

Short description: Sit with knees bent and hands behind you. Lift your hips and travel using opposite hands and feet, keeping your hips raised.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 15–20 seconds; take small steps of approximately 15–20 cm.

Short description: Jump your feet apart while raising your arms overhead, then jump back to the starting position. For a lower-impact version, step your feet out instead of jumping.
Hold a bar overhead while lowering into a squat, then stand.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 5 controlled technique repetitions with a light training bar.

Short description: Lift a barbell overhead in one movement and receive it without a deep squat.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3–5 technique repetitions with an unloaded training bar, under qualified instruction.
Equipment needed: Training bar or barbell; suitable lifting area

Short description: Keep one foot off the floor as you squat, move into a plank, return to the squat, and jump. Repeat on the other leg.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 1 set of 3–5 repetitions per side, only if proficient in regular burpees and single-leg balance.

Short description: Lift a barbell from the floor to overhead in one continuous movement, receiving it in a squat before standing.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: 3–5 technique repetitions with an unloaded training bar, under qualified instruction.
Equipment needed: Training bar or barbell; suitable lifting area

Activity Name: Plank With Elbows on a Stability Ball
Short description: Place your forearms on a stability ball and extend into a plank, keeping your shoulders and hips level. Hold, then lower your knees to rest. Small elbow circles are an optional progression.
Dose (number or repetitions or how long: Hold for up to 10 seconds per repetition; 3–5 sets of 8–12 repetitions.
Equipment needed: Stability ball; optional mat for knees

Equipment needed: Two floor markers; clear space approximately 3–5 metres long
